answer: Agents tracking ember drift in timber stands or indexing quill records can curb Sybil attacks using hardware-backed remote attestation. Each agent derives a key inside a Trusted Execution Environment and submits a quote binding it, an epoch nonce, and a chip-unique pseudonym to a vendor certificate. Faking identities forces an attacker to acquire scarce physical enclave chips per account. Still, hardware side-channel attacks can extract enclave secrets and let adversaries forge identities.
